mainTopic: When 'the actions prove' an offering's identity (מעשיה מוכיחין עליה), so that wrong intent does not stop it from counting: מנחות, bird offerings, and the visible features of animals
overview: רבה explained רבי שמעון's view this way: a מנחה brought with the wrong intent still counts for its owner when its actions clearly show what it really is (מעשיה מוכיחין עליה). This amud tests that idea again and again. A bird offering's blood rites are not always clear proof, but when they are, רבה says the bird offering counts too, because רבי שמעון only contrasted מנחות with animal offerings. The place where an animal was slaughtered, north or south, proves nothing, because onlookers could think the כהן did something wrong. The גמרא then asks whether the same doubt applies to the pan of a מנחה. It answers that, for רבי שמעון, the pan actually used always decides what the מנחה is. Next the גמרא tries animal features one by one: gender, age, and wool versus hair. Each time it explains that people do not notice the difference, or could easily be mistaken. Finally, for a calf or bull slaughtered as a פסח or אשם, the mistake is impossible to miss, and the גמרא agrees that such an offering does count. That sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Squeezing above could be mistaken for the squeezing that follows sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that squeezing blood above the line does not prove the bird is an עולת העוף, because people might think it is a חטאת whose blood was already sprinkled below and is now being squeezed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Perhaps it is the squeezing that comes after sprinkling. As the Master said: If he squeezed its blood anywhere on the altar, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the question raised just before this: why doesn't a bird עולה squeezed above the line for the sake of a חטאת count as a case where 'the actions prove'? It answers that the action is not clear proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird חטאת has its blood sprinkled below the line, and afterward the leftover blood is squeezed out. That later squeezing is valid anywhere on the מזבח, even above the line. So an onlooker who sees squeezing above might think it is a חטאת, and the action does not clearly show it is an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezing the blood out of the bird against the altar wall
Sprinkling the blood
Perhaps; maybe people will think
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: Squeezing above the line is normally the sign of an עולת העוף. The trick here is that a חטאת also has a squeezing step, done after the sprinkling, and that squeezing may be done anywhere on the מזבח.

phrases.english: They answer: People might say, perhaps
it is the squeezing that comes after sprinkling,
as the Master said:
If he squeezed its blood in any place
on the altar, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: דִּילְמָא מִיצּוּי דְּבָתַר הַזָּאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised just before this text about a bird עולה squeezed above the line for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the action is ambiguous, so 'the actions prove' does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Squeezing above the line clearly marks the bird as an עולה, so the wrong intent should not disqualify it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Squeezing above could also be the squeezing a חטאת gets after sprinkling, so it is not clear proof and the wrong intent disqualifies.

steps.title: A bird חטאת sprinkled below for the sake of an עולה should be valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה: a bird חטאת sprinkled below the line, with intent for an עולת העוף, should be valid, because sprinkling below clearly shows it is a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird חטאת whose blood he sprinkled below for the sake of a bird עולה should effect acceptance, since its actions prove it is a bird חטאת. For if it were a bird עולה, he would have done it above, and he would have done squeezing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite case, where the action really is clear proof. By רבה's logic this bird offering should count, but רבי שמעון seems to treat it like an animal offering, where wrong intent stops it from counting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here nothing is ambiguous. An עולת העוף is never done below and never with sprinkling, so sprinkling below can only mean a חטאת. If 'the actions prove' is the rule, this bird offering should be fully valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird sin offering; its blood is sprinkled below the red line
Bird burnt offering; its blood is squeezed above the red line
Its actions prove what it is
Below / above the red line on the altar
It should effect acceptance (count for the owner)

phrases.english: A bird sin offering whose blood he sprinkled below
for the sake of a bird burnt offering should effect acceptance,
since its actions prove about it
that it is a bird sin offering,
for if it were a bird burnt offering,
he would have done it above,
and he would have done squeezing!

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף שֶׁהִזָּה דָּמָהּ לְמַטָּה לְשֵׁם עוֹלַת הָעוֹף תְּרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from an unclear bird case to a clear one, to test רבה's principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that רבי שמעון validates offerings whose actions prove their identity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sprinkling below can only be done for a חטאת, so by רבה's reasoning this bird offering should be valid even though it was brought with the wrong intent.

steps.title: Yes, it is valid; רבי שמעון only contrasted מנחות with animal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the point: such a bird offering really is valid according to רבי שמעון. When he said מנחות are unlike זבחים, he meant animal offerings, not birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, it is so. Rather, he said 'because meal offerings are not similar to slaughtered offerings', meaning to slaughtered offerings, and not to birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by agreeing: yes, this bird offering is valid. רבי שמעון's contrast was never meant to include bird offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that מנחות differ from זבחים. The challenge assumed that birds fall on the זבחים side, where wrong intent disqualifies. The answer is that 'זבחים' means only slaughtered animals, so birds can work like מנחות, where clear actions keep the offering valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, that is true (agreeing with the challenge)
Meal offerings
Slaughtered animal offerings
Bird offerings

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, רבי שמעון's contrast between מנחות and זבחים covers only animal offerings. A bird offering whose actions clearly show what it is stays valid despite the wrong intent.

phrases.english: Indeed, it is so,
rather, 'because meal offerings are not'
'similar to slaughtered offerings' is what he said,
phrases.notes: These are רבי שמעון's own words, which רבה is explaining.

phrases.english: to slaughtered offerings, and not to birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין הַמְּנָחוֹת דּוֹמוֹת לַזְּבָחִים קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge's result and narrows the meaning of רבי שמעון's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the point (הכי נמי) and narrows the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds fall under 'זבחים', so wrong intent should disqualify them even when the actions are clear.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זבחים' means only animal offerings, so a bird offering with clear actions is indeed valid.

steps.title: קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the north for the sake of קדשים קלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new challenge from animal offerings: קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the north with intent for קדשים קלים should be valid, since slaughtering in the north shows they are קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Offerings of the most sacred order that he slaughtered in the north for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity should effect acceptance, since their actions prove they are קדשי קדשים. For if they were קדשים קלים, he would have done them in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a case among animal offerings where the action seems to prove what the offering is, which challenges רבה's claim that animal offerings never have such proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said that for animal offerings, the actions are the same no matter what kind of offering it is, so there is no proof. But קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered in the north, so slaughtering there seems to show which kind it is. By רבה's logic these offerings should then be valid despite the wrong intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most sacred order
Offerings of lesser sanctity
The northern part of the עזרה, where קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered
The southern part of the עזרה
They should effect acceptance

phrases.english: Offerings of the most sacred order that he slaughtered in the north
for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity should effect acceptance,
since their actions prove about them
that they are offerings of the most sacred order,
for if they were offerings of lesser sanctity,
he would have done them in the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן בַּצָּפוֹן לְשֵׁם קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, לִירַצּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bird cases are settled, it challenges רבה with an animal offering where location seems to prove what the offering is.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that for animal offerings the actions never prove what kind of offering it is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughtering in the north is required only for קדשי קדשים, so it seems to prove what the offering is. By רבה's reasoning, such offerings should be valid even with the wrong intent.

steps.title: Slaughtering in the north proves nothing, because קדשים קלים may be slaughtered anywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the north does not show an offering is קדשי קדשים. The Torah allows קדשים קלים "even" in the south, but never limited them to the south only.
steps.simpleTranslation: True, the Torah said קדשים קלים may be slaughtered even in the south. But did it say only in the south and not in the north? As we learned: their slaughter may be done anywhere in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. Slaughtering in the north is no proof that the animal is קדשי קדשים, because קדשים קלים may also be slaughtered there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 assumed that the north belongs only to קדשי קדשים. The גמרא points out that קדשים קלים are allowed in the south as an extra option, while the north is still permitted for them too. Since both kinds may be slaughtered in the north, the location proves nothing, and the wrong intent still keeps the קרבן from counting for its owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / say it is so (concedes a point before limiting it)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
South / north (parts of the Temple courtyard)
The Temple courtyard
Slaughtering the animal

phrases.english: Granted, the Torah said they may be slaughtered even in the south,
phrases.notes: "They" means קדשים קלים, the offerings of lesser holiness.

phrases.english: but did it say in the south and not in the north?
As we learned: their slaughter may be anywhere in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא אַף בַּדָּרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption that the location is exclusive to one kind of offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughtering in the north shows the animal must be קדשי קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The north is valid for all offerings, so it proves nothing about which kind this one is.

steps.title: Then קדשים קלים slaughtered in the south should be valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the case. Slaughtering in the south seems to prove the animal is קדשים קלים, so wrong intent for קדשי קדשים should not ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, קדשים קלים that someone slaughtered in the south for the sake of קדשי קדשים should be accepted. Their actions prove they are קדשים קלים, because if they were קדשי קדשים, he would have slaughtered them in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again with the opposite case. The north proves nothing, but the south seems to prove a great deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered in the north. Slaughtering in the south should therefore show clearly that the animal is קדשים קלים. By רבי שמעון's rule that clear actions cancel the wrong intent, such a קרבן should be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness
Offerings of the highest holiness, which must be slaughtered in the north
Their actions prove what they are, so the wrong intent does not matter
To be accepted, so the owner fulfills his obligation

phrases.english: Offerings of lesser holiness that he slaughtered in the south
for the sake of the most holy offerings should be accepted,
because their actions prove about them
that they are offerings of lesser holiness,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים – בַּצָּפוֹן הֲוָה עָבֵיד לְהוּ.
phrases.english: for if they were the most holy offerings, he would have done them in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן בַּדָּרוֹם לְשֵׁם קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לִירַצּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts Step 5's answer about the north and challenges using the south instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רבי שמעון's rule of מעשיו מוכיחין does not apply to animal offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The south is only allowed for קדשים קלים, so slaughtering there clearly shows the animal's type. The wrong intent should therefore not disqualify it.

steps.title: People may think he slaughtered קדשי קדשים in the wrong place
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering in the south is not clear proof, because onlookers might think the animal is קדשי קדשים and the כהן did something wrong by slaughtering it in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: People might say they are קדשי קדשים, but he transgressed and slaughtered them in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 6. The south does not prove anything for certain, because it could simply be a mistake or a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An action proves the offering's type only if no one could read it another way. Here an observer could think the כהן broke the rule and slaughtered קדשי קדשים in the south. Since that doubt exists, the action is not a clear proof, and the wrong intent still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: He simply transgressed (did it the wrong way)

phrases.english: They answer: people may say they are the most holy offerings,
and he simply transgressed,
and slaughtered them in the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים נִינְהוּ, וּמִיעְבָּר הוּא דַּעֲבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the proof could be read another way (possible transgression)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughtering in the south proves the animal is קדשים קלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It could be קדשי קדשים slaughtered wrongly, so it proves nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: An action counts as proof only if no observer could explain it as a mistake or a sin.

steps.title: By that logic, a מחבת for the sake of a מרחשת proves nothing either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns Step 7's reasoning against מנחות. People could think the owner vowed a מרחשת but wrongly brought it in a מחבת, so רבי שמעון should not say it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a מחבת offered for the sake of a מרחשת should also be a problem. When the כהן takes the handful for the sake of a מרחשת, someone may say: this man vowed to bring a מרחשת, and the fact that he brings it in a מחבת is because it really is a מרחשת. He just transgressed and brought it in a מחבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. If we worry that people will think someone sinned, that worry should also apply to מנחות, where רבי שמעון says the action proves the type.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a מחבת brought for the sake of a מרחשת is valid, because the kind of pan proves its type. Step 7's logic would say an observer might think it is really a מרחשת brought wrongly in a מחבת. Then the action is not clear proof, and רבי שמעון's ruling seems hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on the last answer)
A flat-pan מנחה
A deep-pan מנחה
The כהן taking a handful from the מנחה
He vowed (to bring a specific kind of מנחה)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is aimed at the מנחה case, where רבי שמעון rules the offering is valid. The animal case has already been explained. The question is now why מנחות are different.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, מַחֲבַת לְשֵׁם מַרְחֶשֶׁת נָמֵי,
phrases.english: If so, a flat-pan offering for the sake of a deep-pan offering too:
when this כהן takes its handful for a deep-pan offering,
one might say: this man vowed a deep-pan offering,
and as for the fact that he brings it in a flat pan,
it really is a deep-pan offering,
and he simply transgressed and brought it in a flat pan!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַחֲבַת לְשֵׁם מַרְחֶשֶׁת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 7 as the basis for a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that a מחבת brought for the sake of a מרחשת is valid because its action proves its type
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an onlooker might assume a transgression, the pan used does not clearly prove the מנחה's type, so the wrong intent should disqualify it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to explain what makes a מנחה's action a real proof when an animal's place of slaughter is not.

steps.title: A pan offering is a pan offering, whatever was vowed
steps.stepSummary: Even if the owner vowed a מרחשת, once he brings it in a מחבת it is a real מחבת offering. So a כהן's intent for מרחשת is clearly false.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, even if he vowed to bring it in a deep pan, once he brings it in a flat pan, it is a flat-pan offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 8. It says the vessel actually used decides what the offering is, not what the owner vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 worried that onlookers would think the owner vowed a מרחשת, so they could not tell that the כהן's intent was wrong. The answer is that it does not matter what was vowed. An offering brought in a מחבת simply is a מחבת offering, so anyone can see that a כהן who thinks 'מרחשת' is plainly wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat pan; a מנחה fried in a flat pan
A deep pan; a מנחה cooked in a deep pan
He vowed, meaning he took on a promise to bring an offering

phrases.english: There, even if he vowed [to bring it] in a deep pan,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the מנחה case from Step 8, where the offering was brought in a flat pan.

phrases.english: when he brings it in a flat pan,
it is a flat-pan [offering].

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, כִּי נָמֵי בְּמַרְחֶשֶׁת נָדַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the מנחה's identity follows the vessel actually used, not the vow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Onlookers might think the owner vowed a מרחשת, so the כהן's intent would not look obviously wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: What was vowed does not matter. A מנחה brought in a מחבת is a מחבת, so wrong intent for מרחשת is clearly false.

steps.title: A משנה shows the offering counts as what was brought
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that if someone vowed one type of pan and brought the other, the offering he brought is valid as what it is, but his vow is still unpaid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone who says, 'It is upon me to bring in a flat pan,' and brought it in a deep pan, or said 'in a deep pan' and brought it in a flat pan, what he brought, he brought, but he did not fulfill his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up Step 9. The משנה shows that an offering brought in the 'wrong' vessel is still a valid offering of the type actually brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'What he brought, he brought' means the offering is valid as the kind of מנחה it actually is. The vow is a separate matter. The owner still owes what he promised, but that does not change the identity of the offering in front of us. This proves the vessel, not the vow, decides the type.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is upon me': a general promise. If this offering fails, he must bring another
What he brought, he brought: the offering is valid as what it actually is
He did not fulfill his vow, so he still owes the offering he promised

phrases.english: As we learned [in a משנה]: One who says, 'It is upon me [to bring] in a flat pan,'
and he brought it in a deep pan,
[or he said] 'in a deep pan' and brought it in a flat pan,
what he brought, he brought,
phrases.notes: The offering is valid and is treated as the kind he actually brought.

phrases.english: but he did not fulfill his vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן: הָאוֹמֵר ״הֲרֵי עָלַי בְּמַחֲבַת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 9's answer with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a מנחה brought in a מחבת is a מחבת regardless of the vow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (מנחות 102b): 'What he brought, he brought, but he did not fulfill his vow.'

steps.title: But maybe he said 'this one,' which makes it invalid
steps.stepSummary: Onlookers might think the owner said 'this flour is to be brought in a flat pan' and then brought it in a deep pan. The same משנה says that offering is פסולה, so the wrong intent is again not obviously false.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he said, 'This is to be brought in a flat pan,' and he brought it in a deep pan. As we learned: 'This is to be brought in a flat pan' and he brought it in a deep pan, or 'in a deep pan' and he brought it in a flat pan, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 9's answer. It points to a different kind of vow, 'this one,' where bringing the wrong vessel makes the offering invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It is upon me' is a general promise, but 'this one' attaches the promise to a specific portion of flour. The משנה says that if that specific flour is brought in the other vessel, it is פסולה. So onlookers could think this was such a case, the כהן's wrong intent is not obviously false, and רבי שמעון's ruling that it is valid becomes hard again.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; introduces a possibility that weakens the last answer
'This one': the promise is tied to this specific portion of flour
Disqualified; invalid as an offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of promise. With 'upon me' (Step 10), the offering is valid but the vow is still owed. With 'this one' (here), the offering itself is פסולה.

phrases.english: But perhaps he said, 'This is to be brought in a flat pan,'
and he brought it in a deep pan,
as we learned: '[If he said] This is to be brought in a flat pan,'
and he brought it in a deep pan,
[or 'this is to be brought] in a deep pan' and he brought it in a flat pan,
it is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא אָמַר ״זוֹ לְהָבִיא בְּמַחֲבַת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Steps 9 and 10 by raising the 'this one' case.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9's claim that a מחבת offering is always a clear מחבת, which makes the כהן's wrong intent obviously false.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the owner said 'this one,' the offering in the wrong vessel is פסולה. Onlookers could think that happened here, so the wrong intent is not obviously false, and רבי שמעון should not call the offering valid.

steps.title: For רבי שמעון, naming the vessel means nothing
steps.stepSummary: The challenge works only for the רבנן. רבי שמעון holds that even an 'upon me' vow is fulfilled in the other vessel, so the vessel named makes no difference, and 'this one' and 'upon me' are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, that is indeed so. According to רבי שמעון, since he said, 'He has even fulfilled his vow,' it is clear that fixing a vessel means nothing, and it makes no difference whether he said 'this one' or 'upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 11 by agreeing that it is a real problem, but only for the רבנן. For רבי שמעון there is no problem, because he holds that naming a vessel has no effect at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruling that the 'this one' case is פסולה follows the רבנן. רבי שמעון says that even an 'upon me' vow is fulfilled when the other vessel is used, which shows that the vessel the owner named does not bind the offering. So 'this one' brought in the other vessel is also valid, nobody would think the offering is wrong, and the כהן's wrong intent is clearly false.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the רבנן, yes, that is so: the challenge is admitted for them
Evidently; this shows that
Fixing a vessel: the owner naming which pan the מנחה must be made in
It makes no difference

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the vessel the owner names has no power. Whatever pan the מנחה is actually made in decides what it is. That is why a כהן's wrong intent is always clearly false, and the offering stays valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the defense of רבי שמעון's view against the 'onlookers might be confused' argument from Steps 7 and 8. It also shows that a ruling in a משנה can belong to one side, the רבנן, and need not bind רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: According to the רבנן, that is indeed so;

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: according to רבי שמעון, since רבי שמעון said:
'He has even fulfilled his vow,'
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's view in that same משנה, about the 'upon me' case brought in the other pan.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קְבִיעוּתָא דְמָנָא וְלָא כְּלוּם הוּא,
phrases.english: evidently, fixing a vessel is nothing,
and it makes no difference whether he said 'this one,'
or whether he said 'upon me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּנַן הָכִי נָמֵי, לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinions: the challenge holds for the רבנן but not for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the 'this one' case the offering is פסולה, so onlookers could be misled.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, naming a vessel has no effect, so even the 'this one' case is valid, and the כהן's wrong intent remains clearly false.

steps.title: A male עולה slaughtered as a חטאת should count
steps.stepSummary: If the offering's form proves what it is, then a עולה slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת should fully count, since a עולה is male and a חטאת is female.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a burnt offering slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering should be fully accepted, because this one is male and that one is female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the rule further. If the look of an offering can show that a wrong intent is false, the same should be true for animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A עולה is always a male animal, and an individual's חטאת is female. Anyone looking would see that this male animal cannot be a חטאת. So the intent for חטאת should be obviously false, and the עולה should fully count for the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introduces an attack built from the last idea)
Burnt offering (always a male animal)
Sin offering
It should be accepted (fully count for the owner)

phrases.english: But if that is so,
a burnt offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering should be accepted,
phrases.notes: 'Accepted' here means it fully counts and the owner has done his obligation.

phrases.english: since this one is male and that one is female.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule that the offering's form shows a wrong intent is false, from the meal offerings, and applies it to animal offerings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that a wrong intent does not harm when the offering itself shows what it is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gender should show the identity just as the pan type does, so a עולה slaughtered as a חטאת should fully count. But the הלכה is that it does not count for the owner.

steps.title: The נשיא's goat is a male חטאת
steps.stepSummary: Being male does not prove anything, because the שעיר נשיא is a חטאת that is male.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is the goat of the נשיא, which is male, it is not known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a male animal could still be a חטאת, so onlookers cannot tell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every חטאת is female. The נשיא brings a male goat as his חטאת. So a male animal slaughtered as a חטאת does not look obviously wrong, and the wrong intent is not clearly false.

keyTerms.meaning: The male goat brought by the נשיא (Jewish leader) as his sin offering
It is not known (onlookers cannot tell)

phrases.english: Since there is the goat of the נשיא
which is male, it is not known.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא שְׂעִיר נָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by showing that being male does not rule out a חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: a male חטאת exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Male means עולה, so an intent for חטאת is clearly false.
steps.terutzMaskana: A male animal could be the נשיא's חטאת, so the identity is not obvious.

steps.title: What if he named a private person's חטאת
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן said 'for the sake of a private person's חטאת,' which is always female, the נשיא's goat does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'for the sake of an individual's sin offering,' what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Suppose the כהן named a regular person's חטאת, which is never male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נשיא answer only works if the intent was for a חטאת in general. A private person's חטאת is always female. So a male animal plainly cannot be that, and the wrong intent should again be obviously false.

keyTerms.meaning: A private person's sin offering (always female)
What can be said? (the answer does not work here)

phrases.english: If he said: 'for the sake of an individual's sin offering,'
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְשֵׁם חַטַּאת יָחִיד מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case so that the answer of Step 14 no longer applies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer from the נשיא's goat (Step 14)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the intent named a private person's female חטאת, the male animal clearly does not fit, so the intent is obviously false.

steps.title: The reverse case: a female חטאת slaughtered as a עולה
steps.stepSummary: A private person's female חטאת slaughtered for the sake of a עולה should also count, since a עולה is always male.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, an individual's sin offering slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering should be accepted, since a sin offering is female and a burnt offering is male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge. It flips the case around, where the נשיא answer cannot help at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A עולה is never female. So a female animal cannot be a עולה, and the intent for עולה should be obviously false. Then the חטאת should be valid, even though the הלכה is that a חטאת slaughtered for another purpose is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another challenge)

phrases.english: And furthermore, an individual's sin offering
that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering should be accepted,
since a sin offering is female and a burnt offering is male?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ חַטַּאת יָחִיד שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם עוֹלָה תְּרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reverse case to Step 15 that the נשיא's goat cannot answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle of an offering whose form shows its identity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No עולה is female, so a female animal slaughtered as a עולה plainly shows the intent is false. It should therefore be valid, yet it is not.

steps.title: The tail hides the gender
steps.stepSummary: A lamb's gender is hidden by its fat tail, so onlookers cannot see whether it is male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is covered by the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges at once. People cannot easily see the animal's gender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sheep have a thick fat tail that covers the private parts. So the difference between male and female is not visible. A wrong intent based on gender is therefore not obviously false.

keyTerms.meaning: It is covered
The fat tail of a sheep

phrases.english: It is covered by the tail.
phrases.notes: The animal's private parts are hidden under its thick tail, so you can't see if it is male or female.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיכַּסְּיָא בְּאַלְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Steps 15 and 16 together: gender is not visible, so it proves nothing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical observation: the difference cannot be seen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gender clearly shows whether an animal is a עולה or a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tail hides the gender, so onlookers cannot tell.

steps.title: A female goat has no covering tail
steps.stepSummary: The tail answer works for a lamb, but a female goat brought as a חטאת has no such tail, so her gender is visible.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works where he brought a female lamb. If he brought a female goat, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the tail answer. It only fits sheep, not goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A private person may bring a female lamb or a female goat as a חטאת. A goat's short tail does not hide anything. So for a goat, the gender is visible, and the wrong intent should again be obviously false.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out well (for one case, but not another)
Female lamb
Female goat

phrases.english: This works out where he brought a female lamb,
but if he brought a female goat, what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח הֵיכָא דְּאַיְיתִי כִּבְשָׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of Step 17 to sheep and challenges it for goats.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A goat's gender is not hidden, so in a goat חטאת the wrong intent would be obviously false.

steps.title: People don't pay attention to gender
steps.stepSummary: The real reason is that people simply do not notice whether an offering is male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between males and females is not on people's minds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the tail answer and gives a broader one. Onlookers just do not look at the animal's gender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the gender could be seen, people watching an offering do not check it. So gender is not something that makes the identity obvious. That is why a wrong intent based on gender still harms the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not on people's minds (they don't notice it)
Males and females

steps.whatToRemember: Gender never proves an animal offering's identity, because people do not pay attention to it. So a wrong intent between עולה and חטאת is not 'obviously false.'

phrases.english: Rather, between males and females
is not on people's minds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּין זְכָרִים לִנְקֵבוֹת לָאו אַדַּעְתַּיְיהוּ דְאִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the tail answer with a general answer that covers goats too.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement answer based on what people notice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Visible gender would make the identity obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: People don't look at gender at all, so it never proves the identity.

steps.title: A one-year פסח slaughtered as a two-year אשם
steps.stepSummary: A פסח slaughtered for the sake of an אשם should be accepted, since a פסח is one year old and an אשם is two years old.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסח that one slaughtered for the sake of an אשם should be accepted, since this one is one year old and that one is two years old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from the animal's age instead of its gender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח must be in its first year, while a regular אשם is a ram in its second year. Age seems easy to tell apart. So the intent for אשם should be obviously false, and the פסח should be valid, even though a פסח slaughtered for another purpose is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסח offering (must be within its first year)
Guilt offering (usually a ram in its second year)
In its first year
In its second year

phrases.english: A פסח that one slaughtered for the sake of a guilt offering should be accepted,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהַאי בֶּן שָׁנָה, וְהַאי בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: since this one is in its first year, and that one is in its second year.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֶּסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ לְשֵׁם אָשָׁם לִירַצֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the gender challenges are answered, a new challenge comes from age.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle of an offering whose form shows its identity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Age should show the identity, so the intent for אשם is obviously false and the פסח should be valid. But it is not.

steps.title: Some אשם offerings are also one year old
steps.stepSummary: The אשם of a נזיר and the אשם of a מצורע are one-year-old lambs, so a young animal could still be an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is the אשם of a נזיר and the אשם of a מצורע, it is not clear-cut to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that age does not prove anything here, because some אשם offerings are also young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם of a נזיר and the אשם of a מצורע are both lambs in their first year. So a young animal slaughtered as an אשם does not look wrong to onlookers. The wrong intent is not obviously false, and the פסח is not saved.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering of a נזיר (a lamb in its first year)
The guilt offering of a מצורע (a lamb in its first year)
It is not clear-cut to him (the onlooker cannot be sure)

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא אֲשַׁם נָזִיר וַאֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע,
phrases.english: Since there is the guilt offering of a נזיר and the guilt offering of a מצורע,
phrases.notes: See במדבר 6:12 and ויקרא 14:10. Both of these are lambs in their first year.

phrases.english: it is not clear-cut to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא אֲשַׁם נָזִיר וַאֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by showing that a one-year-old animal could be an אשם.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: one-year-old אשם offerings exist
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being one year old means פסח, so an intent for אשם is clearly false.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם of a נזיר and of a מצורע are also one year old, so onlookers cannot be sure.

steps.title: What if he named a two-year-old guilt offering?
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 21 works for an אשם נזיר or אשם מצורע, but what if the person said he was slaughtering the פסח as an אשם גזילות or אשם מעילות? Those must be two years old.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said, "for the sake of an אשם גזילות" or "for the sake of an אשם מעילות," what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Some kinds of אשם can never be a young lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said a one-year-old פסח could pass for an אשם, because some kinds of אשם are one year old. But the אשם גזילות and the אשם מעילות must be two years old. If he named one of those, a one-year-old פסח obviously does not fit the label, so the label should be ignored as plainly false.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering brought by someone who stole and swore falsely about it
Guilt offering for misusing property that belongs to the בית המקדש
What is there to say? (the earlier answer does not cover this)

phrases.english: If he said: "for the sake of a guilt offering for robbery"
or "for the sake of a guilt offering for misuse of sacred property,"
phrases.notes: These two kinds of אשם must come from an animal in its second year, so they cannot be confused with a young lamb.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: ״לְשׁוּם אֲשַׁם גְּזֵילוֹת וּלְשׁוּם אֲשַׁם מְעִילוֹת״, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 21 by naming the kinds of אשם that are not one-year-old.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 21's claim that a one-year-old animal could pass as an אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אשם גזילות and אשם מעילות must be two years old, so a one-year-old פסח labeled as one of these is obviously mislabeled.

steps.title: The reverse case: a two-year-old guilt offering slaughtered as a פסח
steps.stepSummary: Also, an אשם גזילות or אשם מעילות slaughtered as a פסח should be accepted, since a פסח is one year old and these are two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, an אשם גזילות or an אשם מעילות that someone slaughtered for the sake of a פסח should be accepted, since a פסח is one year old and these are two years old!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second question. It flips the case: now the older animal is given the label of the younger offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If age is easy to see, then calling a two-year-old ram a פסח is plainly false. By רבי שמעון's logic, a plainly false label should be ignored, so the offering should count. This strengthens the question by showing the problem goes both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another question)
They should be accepted (count for the owner)
An animal in its first year
An animal in its second year

phrases.english: And furthermore, a guilt offering for robbery and a guilt offering for misuse
that one slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering should be accepted,
since a Paschal offering is in its first year
and these are in their second year!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, אֲשַׁם גְּזֵילוֹת וַאֲשַׁם מְעִילוֹת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשׁוּם פֶּסַח לִירַצּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, reverse version of the challenge in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that these offerings are not visibly different
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If age difference is visible, a two-year-old labeled as a one-year-old פסח is obviously false, so the offering should be accepted.

steps.title: People cannot tell one-year-olds from two-year-olds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier answer and says people do not notice the difference between first-year and second-year animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, people do not pay attention to the difference between a one-year-old and a two-year-old, because some one-year-olds look two, and some two-year-olds look one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that covers both questions. Age is not something onlookers can see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the גמרא is leaving behind the answer of step 21 (the young אשם of a נזיר or מצורע). Instead it says age is not a visible feature, since animals of different ages can look alike. So a wrong label about age is not obviously false, and the normal rule applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer for a new one)
People do not pay attention to it
Looks like

phrases.english: Rather, between one in its first year
and one in its second year
people do not pay attention,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיכָּא בֶּן שָׁנָה דְּמִיחֲזֵי כְּבֶן שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: for there is one in its first year that looks like one in its second,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיכָּא בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם דְּמִיחֲזֵי כְּבֶן שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: and there is one in its second year that looks like one in its first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בֵּין בֶּן שָׁנָה לְבֵין בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים לָאו אַדַּעְתַּיְיהוּ דְאִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers steps 22 and 23 by replacing the answer of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual claim: the difference is not visible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Age difference is obvious, so a label about age would be clearly false.
steps.terutzMaskana: Age is not reliably visible, so such a label is not obviously false.
steps.whatToRemember: The question is always whether onlookers can see the label is wrong. Age is not something people can see.

steps.title: A goat has hair, a ram has wool
steps.stepSummary: A goat slaughtered as an אשם should be accepted, since an אשם is a ram with wool and a goat has hair, which anyone can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: A goat that someone slaughtered for the sake of an אשם should be accepted, since this one has wool and that one has hair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from age to species. A goat and a ram look different, so a goat called an אשם seems obviously mislabeled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Age may be hard to see, but wool versus hair seems easy to tell apart. An אשם comes from a ram, which has wool, while a goat has hair. So the label should be plainly false, and the offering should count.

keyTerms.meaning: Goat (here, a goat brought as a חטאת)
Wool (on sheep and rams)
Hair (on goats)

phrases.english: A goat that one slaughtered for the sake of a guilt offering should be accepted,
since this one has wool and that one has hair!
phrases.notes: "This one" is the אשם (a ram, with wool); "that one" is the goat, with hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂעִיר שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ לְשׁוּם אָשָׁם לִירַצֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After age was shown to be invisible, the גמרא tries a visible difference: wool versus hair.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that offerings cannot be told apart by sight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wool versus hair is clearly visible, so a goat labeled as an אשם is obviously false and should be accepted.

steps.title: People think it is a black ram
steps.stepSummary: Onlookers will assume the goat is just a black ram, so the label is not obviously false.
steps.simpleTranslation: People say: it is a black ram.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ordinary people will not see a goat. They will think it is a dark-colored ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between wool and hair is not obvious to a casual onlooker. A black goat can easily be mistaken for a black ram. So a goat labeled as an אשם can still be mistaken for one.

keyTerms.meaning: A black ram

phrases.english: People say: it is a black ram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: דִּיכְרָא אוּכָּמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual claim about how people perceive the animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wool versus hair makes a goat obviously not an אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: People will think it is a black ram, so the label is not obviously false.

steps.title: A calf or bull could never be a פסח or אשם
steps.stepSummary: A calf or bull slaughtered as a פסח or אשם should be accepted, because neither offering is ever brought from cattle.
steps.simpleTranslation: A calf or a bull that someone slaughtered for the sake of a פסח or an אשם should be accepted, since there is no calf or bull among פסח and אשם offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case where the mistake cannot be hidden. A פסח or an אשם is never brought from cattle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one could mistake a calf or bull for a lamb or ram. So labeling cattle as a פסח or אשם is obviously false. By the rule, the offering should be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Calf
Bull
There is none / does not exist

phrases.english: A calf or a bull that one slaughtered
for the sake of a Paschal offering or a guilt offering should be accepted,
since there is no calf or bull among Paschal and guilt offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵגֶל וּפַר שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשׁוּם פֶּסַח וְאָשָׁם, לִירַצּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the goat case was explained away, the גמרא brings a case that cannot be explained away.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a mislabeled offering is never accepted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cattle can never be a פסח or an אשם, so the label is obviously false and the offering should count.

steps.title: Yes, such an offering is indeed accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: a calf or bull slaughtered as a פסח or אשם really is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not fight the question. It agrees that in this case the offering does count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wrong label is impossible to miss, so the rule fits perfectly. The calf or bull is accepted for its owner. The sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא agrees with the question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a defeat for the סוגיא. The גמרא is agreeing, because the case fits רבי שמעון's rule: an obviously false label is ignored.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by accepting its point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the questioner's conclusion is correct
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the question shows a problem with the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: No problem: cattle labeled as a פסח or אשם are indeed accepted, since the mistake is obvious.
steps.whatToRemember: When the wrong label is impossible to miss, such as cattle called a פסח or אשם, the offering is indeed accepted.
